podcast.title: Career Transition to Chiropractic
podcast.body: After numerous gigs with various bands, Terry Chimes retired from music by 1994 to pursue his passion for biology, medicine, and healing. He opened a chiropractic clinic in Essex, which later expanded into a chain of clinics, and he began giving lectures on alternative medicine. "by 1994, he'd retired from music and opened a chiropractic clinic in Essex."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Multiple Stints with The Clash
podcast.body: Terry Chimes was initially the drummer for The Clash in 1976 and for a period in 1977, appearing on their debut album. He was replaced by Topper Headon in mid-1977 but returned to replace Topper in 1982 and 1983 before leaving for a third time, again replaced by Topper. "He was in the clash a couple of times in 1976 and for a period in 1977, which was long enough for him to appear on that first record."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Spiritual Awakening and Catholicism
podcast.body: Around the turn of the millennium, Dr. Chimes experienced a spiritual awakening that led to a strong devotion to Catholicism. He subsequently began working with the Catholic Church, a significant shift for someone who came up through gritty punk bands and played with Black Sabbath. "Dr. Chimes experienced a spiritual awakening around the turn of the millennium, prompting a strong devotion to Catholicism and working with the Catholic Church."

xref.title: Terry Chimes' Career Change to Healthcare
xref.body: After a successful music career with The Clash, Generation X, and Black Sabbath, Terry Chimes began to rethink his path in the late 1980s. Influenced by his experiences with the rock and roll lifestyle, he concluded that "the natural way of healing is far better than pumping people full of drugs." This led him to adopt a meat- and alcohol-free lifestyle, study chiropractic medicine at various schools across the UK, and learn acupuncture in China. "But by the end of the 1980s, Terry began thinking about doing something else."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
